# Independent audit: facet-free global maximizer hull

Audited `candidate 36faf5655458d282` in full,
using the previously audited finite-tilt attainment and ambient facet-flux
lemmas. The theorem passes under its stated `d>=2`, positive mixed-volume,
and zero supporting `(d-1)`-measure hypotheses.

* Strict exclusion is valid in both cases. If another maximum is strictly
inside an active cap, translating its boundary through that point removes
a positive own-fiber slab. If it lies on the boundary, the ambient-affine
facet-flux lemma applies even when the two bases agree. Its left side is
positive because a nonvertical cut through a fiber interior has a positive
proper section; its right side vanishes by the supporting-section assumption.
* The integer-combination argument uses the quasiconcavity of actual
halfspace depth, not fiberwise or marginal depth. Every halfspace containing
a convex combination contains at least one positively weighted source
point. If the combination has integer base, it is therefore itself a global
maximum. Its active cap cannot have zero average margin when every distinct
source maximum is strictly excluded. This proves injectivity, convex
position, the empty integer hull, and the parity bound without an
unjustified assumption about continuous-base centers.
* The saturation argument in uniform separation preserves the second
point exactly. Its tilt evaluation has a finite limit because its margin
tends to zero and the unit continuous normals converge. It therefore
belongs to the finite-limit index set. The limiting evaluations on their
span are consistent by linearity, and replacing the span projection fixes
ALL these evaluations simultaneously. Divergent evaluations retain their
signs after the bounded replacement; one finite sufficiently late tilt
fully saturates every such bounded fiber. Finite-limit cap masses converge
because their continuous normal remains nonzero. The resulting finite cap
has mass `beta M` and passes through both maxima, giving the required
contradiction. No compactness of the integer tilts was presumed.
* Unit continuous normals convert the uniform negative margins into fixed
excluded continuous balls. These balls can be decreased to lie in the
other positive fibers. Finiteness of the maximizer set then allows one
common radius for the fixed body, without any uniformity over bodies.
* A positive balanced circuit cancels the continuous terms exactly. Its
weighted integer normal has strictly negative evaluation at every other
maximizing base, so it genuinely exposes the chosen base. For a singleton,
the statement is correctly vacuous.

The final scope limitation is essential: neither the parity bound nor
strict active-cap exclusion survives automatically under a faceted limit,
and neither supplies the missing mixed-volume allocation or OC constant.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
